name: GstarCAD Architecture
tagline: Architectural drawing environment with wall/door/window style objects and project-oriented layer conventions.
meta_desc: Suited to building plans, elevations, and construction documentation when you want DWG-based AEC tools rather than a full BIM database. Coordinate deliverables with project partners on expected object types and export formats.

terms.title: Architectural Object Styles
terms.short_def: Technical best practices for Architectural Object Styles inside GstarCAD Architecture.
terms.definition: Architectural Object Styles define parametric properties for walls, doors, windows, and slabs. They represent smart objects carrying dimensions and structural layers.
terms.why_matters: Speeds up plan modeling and ensures elements render consistently in 3D orthographic views.
common_pitfalls: Exploding smart architectural objects into raw 2D lines, which breaks all parametric updates
Mixing different wall styles on the same floor level causing display issues

quiz.question: When working with Architectural Object Styles, which of the following represents a common technical pitfall?
options: Exploding smart architectural objects into raw 2D lines, which breaks all parametric updates.
Failing to manually re-index the SQL server database.
Over-allocating virtual memory caches in the cloud settings.
Restricting linetype scales strictly to 1:1 paper coordinates.
quiz.explanation: Correct. A common pitfall is 'Exploding smart architectural objects into raw 2D lines, which breaks all parametric updates.' As the editorial review notes: 'Speeds up plan modeling and ensures elements render consistently in 3D orthographic views.'

terms.title: Project Elevation Generator
terms.short_def: Technical best practices for Project Elevation Generator inside GstarCAD Architecture.
terms.definition: The Project Elevation Generator projects 2D floor plans into 3D elevations and sectional cuts, keeping drawings in sync.
terms.why_matters: Saves hours of drafting and ensures spatial consistency across plan layouts and elevations.
common_pitfalls: Generating elevations without configuring the correct height baseline first
Neglecting to update elevation views after changing floor plan partitions

quiz.question: When working with Project Elevation Generator, which of the following represents a common technical pitfall?
options: Generating elevations without configuring the correct height baseline first.
Failing to manually re-index the SQL server database.
Over-allocating virtual memory caches in the cloud settings.
Restricting linetype scales strictly to 1:1 paper coordinates.
quiz.explanation: Correct. A common pitfall is 'Generating elevations without configuring the correct height baseline first.' As the editorial review notes: 'Saves hours of drafting and ensures spatial consistency across plan layouts and elevations.'

terms.title: Grid Alignment Setup
terms.short_def: Technical best practices for Grid Alignment Setup inside GstarCAD Architecture.
terms.definition: Grid Alignment Setup places structural grids and reference bubbles, locking drawing origins relative to the coordinate base.
terms.why_matters: Maintains model coordinate control across structural, MEP, and architectural drawing sheets.
common_pitfalls: Moving grid lines manually without locking parallel constraints
Having origin offsets between architectural grids and structural engineering coordinates

faqs.question: How do I create custom wall styles?
faqs.answer: Open the Style Manager, select Wall Styles, click New, define wall layers (material, thickness, offset), and save the style to your templates.

faqs.question: Can I generate 3D models from 2D architectural plans?
faqs.answer: Yes. Wall, door, and window elements in GstarCAD Architecture are intelligent 3D elements that automatically render in 3D when switching the viewpoint.

faqs.question: How do I export architectural models to IFC?
faqs.answer: Use the `IFCEXPORT` command, map GstarCAD Architecture layers to standard IFC classes, and save the coordinates relative to the project base point.
